The vibe is family-feel and outdoorsy combining traditional warmth with forward-thinking approaches.

Swanbourne punches well above its weight when it comes to sport.
This Is Swanbourne Spirit
One of the most well renowned independent prep schools near Milton Keynes and across the region, we combine academic ambition with exceptional pastoral care, a rich co-curricular programme and a strong sense of community.
Whether you’re looking for a co-educational day prep school, an independent school nursery or a top boarding school, Swanbourne House provides an innovative education delivered in an inspiring setting where every child can thrive.
Kindness, Effort & Curiosity
With a proud history of preparing pupils for a fulfilling, productive and happy life, our vision is to deliver a joyous education that lays the foundations for lifelong discovery, curiosity, health and wellbeing. We aim to equip children for a future full of opportunity, inspiration, enjoyment and purpose. This is the Swanbourne Spirit.
Nick Holloway, Head at Swanbourne House

Our pupils are artists, athletes, musicians, performers, scientists and explorers. They are kind, inquisitive, brave, bursting with potential, prepared to take risks and are encouraged to be themselves. Whether they are mastering a tricky maths concept, performing on stage, playing for a team, putting themselves out of their comfort zone or holding a door open for a friend, every success – big or small – is celebrated.

pageCache.pageTitle: The Swanbourne Journey - Swanbourne House School
pageCache.text:
Book a visit
Choosing the right school is a big decision — and there’s no better way to get a feel for Swanbourne than by visiting in person. Complete the form below and we’ll arrange a tour and meeting with our Head at a time that suits your family.
The Swanbourne Journey
The Swanbourne Journey
At Swanbourne House, we are proud of our strong academic tradition and the breadth of opportunity we offer every pupil. However, we also recognise that the world our children are preparing for is changing at an unprecedented pace. The expectations of parents, senior schools and future employers continue to evolve. While academic excellence remains central, there is now greater importance placed on communication, critical thinking, collaboration, creativity and leadership, alongside strong subject knowledge.
Success is no longer defined solely by what pupils know, but by how effectively they can apply that knowledge – how they question, explore and adapt.
It is this belief that underpins The Swanbourne Journey – our approach to developing young people from age 3 to 13.
Our ambition is simple: that every pupil leaves Swanbourne House fully prepared for senior school and ready to thrive in a rapidly changing world.
Deputy Head Academic
Scholarship and academic excellence have long been hallmarks of Swanbourne House. Through high expectations, specialist teaching and a culture of ambition, pupils are supported and challenged to achieve their full potential and encouraged to pursue excellence and develop a genuine love of learning.
The Swanbourne Journey provides a coherent pathway from Pre-reception to Year 8, combining strong academic foundations with opportunities for personal growth, leadership and intellectual challenge.
FOUNDATIONS FOR SUCCESS (age 3 to 8)
Through a broad and engaging curriculum, pupils develop secure foundations in literacy, numeracy and learning behaviours. Underpinned by our Swanbots skills programme, they build the confidence, curiosity and independence required for future success.
THE SWANBOURNE PATHWAY (age 9 to 13)
The Swanbourne Pathway combines three key elements that work together to prepare pupils for senior school and beyond.
Academic Excellence
Signature Skills
Signature Experiences
THE SWANBOURNE CERTIFICATE
The Certificate captures the last two years of the Swanbourne Pathway (Years 7 & 8, ages 11 to 13), celebrating achievement across the academic and wider curriculum while recognising growth, contribution and personal development.
SIGNATURE SKILLS
The Swanbourne Signature Skills provide a common language through which pupils can understand, reflect upon and articulate their growth. They are not taught as standalone lessons but are woven throughout the curriculum and wider life of the school, providing opportunities for pupils to develop and demonstrate them in meaningful contexts.
These are the essential human skills that enable pupils to thrive in an increasingly digital and AI-driven society.
The ability to communicate ideas clearly, confidently and purposefully.
At Swanbourne, pupils develop Oracy through presentations, debates, discussions, viva-style assessments and public speaking opportunities. Whether explaining a scientific investigation, defending an argument in History or presenting findings from the Independent Enquiry Project, pupils learn to communicate with confidence.
Asking thoughtful questions and seeking deeper understanding.
Pupils develop Enquiry through research, investigation and exploration. From evaluating historical sources and conducting scientific investigations to undertaking independent projects, pupils learn to question, analyse
and think critically.
Working effectively with others to achieve a shared goal.
Through team projects, practical investigations, performances and sporting activities, pupils learn to listen, contribute, adapt and support others whilst working towards a common purpose.
Generating ideas, solving problems and thinking innovatively.
Creativity is developed across the curriculum. Whether designing a prototype in DT, creating a solution as part of the Innovate Project, composing music or approaching a problem from a different perspective, pupils are encouraged to think imaginatively and take intellectual risks.
Taking responsibility, showing initiative and positively influencing others.
Pupils develop Leadership through positions of responsibility, mentoring opportunities, collaborative projects and wider school involvement. They learn to lead by example, make considered decisions and contribute positively to their community.
Demonstrating perseverance, commitment and a willingness to embrace challenge.
Endeavour underpins everything we do. Pupils are encouraged to respond positively to feedback, tackle difficult tasks with determination and recognise that growth often comes through challenge and persistence.
COLLABORATION
LEADERSHIP
ENDEAVOUR
SIGNATURE EXPERIENCES
A Swanbourne education goes far beyond the classroom. Through a range of Signature Experiences, pupils apply their learning to creative and real-world contexts, harnessing curiosity and independence along the way.
Our expansive grounds provide space to explore, create and discover, while our location – close to Milton Keynes and the Oxford–Cambridge technology arc – connects pupils to one of the UK’s most dynamic centres of innovation.
As part of The Stowe Group, pupils also benefit from access to Stowe’s outstanding teaching and learning facilities.
Year 7 Innovate Project
This project challenges pupils to think differently… and think bigger.
Through research, planning, design, prototyping and presentation, they experience the interconnected nature of Science, Technology, Engineering and Maths (STEM) subjects whilst developing creativity, resilience and problem-solving skills.
Year 8 Independent Enquiry Project
The Independent Enquiry Project provides pupils with the opportunity to pursue a subject of personal interest in depth and take ownership of their learning.
Through sustained research and investigation, pupils learn to formulate questions, evaluate evidence, think critically and communicate their findings with confidence. They develop the habits of scholarship, intellectual curiosity and independent thinking that will support success at senior school and beyond.
As part of the project, pupils are taught to engage critically with emerging technologies, including artificial intelligence, learning to question sources, identify bias and develop informed, independent viewpoints.
Year 7 & 8 Potential Scholars Group
Potential Scholars Groups in Years 7 and 8 provide opportunities for pupils to pursue their interests and
talents beyond the curriculum, preparing them specifically for the scholarship processes at senior schools.
Through specialist mentoring, enrichment and challenge across Academics, Sport, Music,
Drama, Art and Design Technology, pupils delve deeper into their interests, developing
curiosity and a drive for excellence.
Horizons
Horizons brings learning to life beyond the classroom.
Through residential trips, outdoor learning, visiting speakers, cultural experiences and moments of reflection, pupils are encouraged to develop a sense of awe and wonder about the world around them. Experiences might range from hearing first-hand accounts from an Arctic explorer, to taking part in a STEM roadshow, or experiencing the adventure and teamwork of the Combined Cadet Force.
Leadership and Responsibility
Through positions of responsibility, mentoring and wider school involvement, pupils are encouraged to demonstrate initiative, support others and make a positive contribution to the school community and local area. These experiences help pupils develop the confidence, character and leadership qualities that will serve them throughout their lives.
FAQ
What is The Swanbourne Journey?
The Swanbourne Journey is our educational pathway from Pre-Reception to Year 8. It combines strong academic foundations with personal development, leadership opportunities and real-world learning experiences, ensuring pupils are fully prepared for senior school and beyond.
What makes the Swanbourne curriculum different?
The Swanbourne Journey combines three key elements: Academic Excellence, Signature Skills and Signature Experiences. Alongside a rigorous and ambitious curriculum, pupils develop the six Swanbourne Signature Skills: Oracy, Enquiry, Collaboration, Creativity, Leadership and Endeavour – and have opportunities to apply their learning through meaningful real-world experiences.
What are the Swanbourne Signature Skills?
The Signature Skills are:
These skills are embedded throughout the curriculum and wider school life. Together, they help pupils develop the confidence, independence and adaptability they need to thrive at senior school and in an increasingly digital world.
What are Signature Experiences?
Signature Experiences are distinctive opportunities that allow pupils to apply their learning beyond the classroom. These include the Year 7 Innovate Project, the Year 8 Independent Enquiry Project, the Potential Scholars Programme, leadership opportunities, outdoor learning, visiting speakers and residential experiences.
These experiences encourage pupils to explore their interests, embrace challenge, work with others and discover what they are capable of achieving.
Why does The Swanbourne Journey focus on skills as well as academic knowledge?
We believe future success depends on more than academic results alone. Oracy, enquiry, collaboration, creativity, leadership and endeavour help pupils adapt to new challenges, work effectively with others and apply their learning confidently in the real world.
These qualities are deliberately developed throughout The Swanbourne Journey, both within the curriculum and through the wider life of the school.
How does Swanbourne prepare pupils for a world shaped by AI?
We believe that strong academic knowledge must be complemented by the human skills that are increasingly important in a technology-rich world.
Through the Swanbourne Signature Skills, pupils develop creativity, enquiry, collaboration, leadership, oracy and endeavour. As they progress through the school, pupils also learn to use technology thoughtfully and responsibly, including critically evaluating AI-generated content, recognising potential bias, questioning sources and developing their own independent judgement.
What role does STEM play in The Swanbourne Journey?
STEM is an important strand of The Swanbourne Journey. From an early age, pupils encounter opportunities in coding, robotics, scientific investigation, design, engineering and problem-solving. As they progress through the school, these experiences become increasingly sophisticated, culminating in opportunities such as the Year 7 Innovate Project, where pupils bring together science, technology, engineering and creativity to solve authentic problems.
What is the Swanbourne Certificate?
The Swanbourne Certificate is awarded at the end of Year 8 and provides a holistic profile of each pupil’s achievements, strengths and contributions throughout the final stage of their Swanbourne Journey. It recognises academic attainment, contribution across the wider curriculum, Signature Skills and Signature Experiences, capturing a much broader picture of success than traditional examinations alone.
How are pupils assessed throughout The Swanbourne Journey?
Assessment is an important part of The Swanbourne Journey and takes a range of forms as pupils progress through the school. Teachers use regular assessment to understand pupils’ progress, identify areas for development and ensure appropriate challenge. In Years 7 and 8, pupils also sit formal internal examinations in examined subjects, alongside other assessment opportunities across the curriculum. This ensures that pupils are well prepared for the expectations of senior school while allowing us to recognise achievement more broadly through the Swanbourne Certificate.
How does Swanbourne prepare pupils for senior school?
Academic preparation sits at the heart of The Swanbourne Journey. Pupils develop strong subject knowledge alongside increasingly sophisticated learning habits, independence and intellectual curiosity. Alongside this academic rigour, pupils have opportunities to lead, collaborate, communicate, solve problems and pursue their individual strengths.
Pupils leave Swanbourne with the knowledge, skills, confidence and independence to make the most of life at their chosen senior school.
Will The Swanbourne Journey be recognised by senior schools?
Yes. We work closely with senior schools to understand their individual entry requirements and ensure that Swanbourne pupils are fully prepared for any examinations, assessments or interviews required as part of the admissions process.
The Swanbourne Journey provides a rigorous academic curriculum and does not limit pupils’ senior-school options or destinations. Where a senior school has specific entry or scholarship requirements, pupils receive tailored preparation to ensure they are ready.
Does Swanbourne House support scholarship candidates?
Yes. Our Potential Scholars Programme in Years 7 and 8 provides specialist mentoring, enrichment and challenge for pupils with the potential to pursue scholarships across academic, sport, music, drama, art and design technology. Pupils receive targeted preparation and opportunities to extend their strengths, helping them approach senior-school scholarship applications and assessments with confidence.
What opportunities do pupils have through The Stowe Group?
Being part of The Stowe Group gives Swanbourne pupils access to exceptional facilities, expertise and opportunities beyond our own site.
These include opportunities to use facilities such as the Howden Design Centre, Worsley Science Centre, Roxburgh Theatre and Chung Music School, alongside specialist experiences in areas including science, engineering, coding,

We know how busy family life can be, which is why we offer flexible wraparound care to support you and your child, providing a safe, happy environment beyond the core school day.

Latin & Modern Foreign Languages
Modern Languages
At Swanbourne House, we foster a love of languages and global cultures from an early age. From Year 1, pupils enjoy a weekly French lesson filled with songs, rhymes and simple vocabulary. By Years 7 and 8, pupils have three French lessons per week, with some preparing for 13+ Scholarship papers as part of the PSB curriculum. All skills are assessed from Year 5 onwards, ensuring a strong focus on practical communication and positive learning experiences. In addition, pupils in Year 7 can opt to learn Spanish as part of the curriculum.
Experiencing the language
In Year 7, pupils take part in a week of French immersion in Normandy at Château de la Baudonnière, where they enjoy a wide range of outdoor activities conducted entirely in French.
We also collaborate with a French theatre company to deliver interactive performances for Years 5 and 6, while Year 4 pupils practise their French in real-life situations during a visit to a French shop. As part of the Year 8 Leavers’ Programme, pupils engage in a variety of challenging language-based activities designed to introduce them to languages at Senior School level.
We also have strong links with the MFL department at Stowe School, including a trip for Year 8 to watch French and Spanish theatre productions.
Learning other modern languages
To promote a passion for languages beyond French, we introduce Spanish and Mandarin clubs from Year 1, with both available as individual or small group tuition from Year 3 onwards.
Our Language Ambassador programme enables pupils to share their enthusiasm for languages and cultures through collaborative projects that develop their leadership skills. Pupils are also encouraged to enter the UK Junior Language Challenge, an interactive national competition which inspires them to explore new languages in a fun and engaging way.
Latin
A cultural appreciation for the ancient world and our place in its wake is developed through the study of Latin. Pupils begin Latin at Swanbourne House in Year 5 with one lesson a week, followed by two a week from Year 6 onwards. Initially, they learn the foundational principles of grammar which have a direct impact on their English and any other languages they may go on to study.
They also explore topics within Classical Civilisation in order to enrich their contextual understanding of Latin, and appreciate its usefulness in connection to the language’s historical, literary and cultural importance.
Pupils are taught up to 13+ Scholarship level proficiency in Latin, and after their exams also delve into foundational Ancient Greek. Field trips are also organised, such as the Year 8 Leavers trip to the Ashmoleon, and Year 6 exploring mythological themes through the temples of Stowe.

Independent Schools Inspection Reports
ISI is an independent inspectorate, appointed by the Department for Education to inspect association independent schools in England.
Read our latest Independent Schools Inspection Report.
Some of the findings of the report include:
“Leaders provide a broad curriculum that effectively prepares pupils for the next stage of their eduction. Pupils understand and apply core skills such as collaboration and independence and review and improvement.”
“Pupils engage positively in their learning and respond well to the challenging tasks posed by teachers.”
“Pupils display a common mutual respect for all members of the school community. Highly positive relationships between pupils and staff enhance the learning environment.”
“Pupils respond positively to praise, and they value the reward system which recognises the effort they show in their learning.”
“Pupils understand the importance of good mental and physical health. School leaders provide an extensive range of co-curricular activities for pupils which increase their self-esteem and self-confidence and prepare them well for the next steps in their eduction.”

Drama
Productions at Swanbourne House
Drama at Swanbourne House
With a dedicated drama room and specialist teaching throughout the school, every pupil is encouraged to express themselves creatively and build confidence on stage. All children have the chance to take on speaking roles, whether in our annual Nativity or smaller, informal productions throughout the year.
Curriculum
Weekly 60-minute lessons inspire passion, creativity, and confidence. Each half term focuses on a new theme, with pupils exploring improvisation, scripted drama, dance, singing, mime, directing and physical theatre. Through this, they gain experience in musical theatre, comedy and characterisation
Productions
Every pupil takes part in at least one production each year, with speaking roles guaranteed from age eight. Younger children perform nativity plays, Years 3 and 4 stage musicals, Year 5 produces classic plays in the outdoor amphitheatre, Year 6 delivers a Shakespeare showcase and Year 7 performs a Christmas pantomime.
Our Senior Musical (open to Years 6+) is staged in the Bridget More Hall with professional-level lighting, sound and a live band. Past productions include Fame, Grease, The Sound of Music, Shrek the Musical, Matilda the Musical, Hairspray and Footloose.
Co-Curricular
Interactive shows and drama workshops visit the School throughout the year and pupils also have the opportunity to experience drama and performance outside of the School with various trips (including to the West End).
We also offer drama clubs, specialist dance classes and a scholarship mentoring programme for those pursuing Performing Arts scholarships.
Drama in The Stowe Group
Being part of The Stowe Group has opened up a wealth of new performing arts opportunities for Swanbourne House pupils. From specialist workshops and masterclasses in music and drama to orchestral days and shared performances – including a recent production of Oliver! and the annual Carol Service.
Swanbourne pupils also have access to the state-of-the-art performing arts facilities at Stowe, including the Cheung Music School with its 200- seat Ugland Auditorium, the Roxburgh Theatre and a professional recording studio.

Maths
Maths at Swanbourne House
At Swanbourne House, mathematics is hands-on, practical and inspiring. Our spiral curriculum builds confidence by returning to key skills at increasing levels of depth, while applying maths to real-life contexts – from designing board games to planning trips.
Specialist Teaching
From Year 5 onwards, pupils are taught by specialist maths teachers in dedicated classrooms. Lessons focus on problem-solving, reasoning and creativity, encouraging children to explore different solutions, explain their thinking and develop resilience.
Broad Skills and Strong Foundations
Pupils cover the full range of topics — including arithmetic, fractions, algebra, geometry and statistics — with an emphasis on making connections and applying knowledge in new situations. A mix of practical tools, visual models and abstract methods ensures every child builds strong, lasting foundations.
Innovation and Technology
Technology is woven into our teaching, with pupils using iPads and interactive apps to explore problems and share their learning. Our department includes a Microsoft and Apple Distinguished Educator, reflecting our innovative use of digital tools to enhance understanding.
Enrichment and Competitions
Pupils are encouraged to stretch themselves through national competitions, including the UK Primary Maths Challenge (Years 5 & 6) and the UK Mathematics Trust Junior Mathematical Challenge (Years 7 & 8). Many achieve success in follow-on rounds such as the Junior Kangaroo and Junior Olympiad.

Music
Music at Swanbourne House
Music is woven into daily life at Swanbourne House, with over 60% of pupils learning an instrument or taking singing lessons — and many mastering more than one. Our approach embraces a wide range of styles, from classical to contemporary, ensuring every pupil has the chance to discover their own musical interests.
Curriculum
Our curriculum balances technical skills with musical expression, encouraging children to explore how music makes them feel.
We have specialists across a range of disciplines and excellent facilities, including a fully equipped music room, several practice spaces and a dedicated Percussion Room. From Year 3 onwards, pupils can take individual lessons on instruments ranging from violin, piano and guitar to harp and drums.
Clubs, Ensembles and Enrichment
Beyond the classroom, pupils can join jazz, string, percussion, brass, and guitar groups, or try songwriting and music technology through Saturday Enrichment. Our Senior Choir performs locally and internationally, with tours to Jersey, Normandy, and the Netherlands in recent years. The Senior Vocal Group offers a selective programme of specialist vocal tuition for older pupils.
Scholarships and Mentoring
For pupils aspiring to music scholarships at Senior School, our mentoring group provides tailored guidance, deepening understanding of advanced techniques and theory.
Performances and Concerts
Performance is central to music at Swanbourne House. Pupils take part in regular concerts, masterclasses and workshops throughout the year (such as the Les Misérables workshop at Stowe, left), gaining confidence and invaluable stage experience.
We also host Christmas and Summer Concerts with a variety of musical disciplines and styles featured, from jazz to classical to rock.

Pastoral Care
Pastoral Care & Wellbeing at Swanbourne House
Pastoral care is the foundation upon which everything at Swanbourne House is built. We place the utmost importance on this vital element of school. Pastoral care is not something else that we add to the plate, it quite simply is the plate.
What does that mean in reality? It is based on strong relationships. The relationships that the children have with each other, the relationships that they have with the adults who work here and the relationship between the school and the parents. These are relationships built on trust and understanding and ones that have dignity at their core.
The pastoral care network is woven through the whole school from class teachers and tutors, the school nurse and houseparents to the estates and domestics teams. We are all here to give your children the best care and keep an eye out for them at all times.
We have robust structures in place to deal with all the ups and downs that are normal when you are educating pupils from 3 to 13 and a strong external team to draw upon should we need to. Good pastoral care is both informative and reactive.
From the classroom to the playing fields, the Wellbeing Hub to the woods, Swanbourne is a community where children are encouraged to grow with confidence, resilience and joy. Our pastoral care helps ensure that every pupil has the support they need to thrive, not just academically, but as happy, healthy, confident young people.
Spaces for Wellbeing
With 55 acres of beautiful grounds, Swanbourne offers pupils unique opportunities for reflection, play and restoration.
The Wellbeing Hub, based in our Boarding House, is a calm and supportive space open at break times. Staffed by our trained Mental Health First Aiders and supported by Wellbeing Prefects from Years 7 and 8, it provides a welcoming environment for any child seeking a moment of pause or connection.
Wellbeing in the Curriculum
Physical and mental wellbeing is woven into daily life at Swanbourne. Our onsite School Nurse is available every day from 8.30am–4.30pm, with an extended presence once a week in the Boarding House until 7.00pm.
Beyond medical care, she delivers PSHE workshops throughout the year, focusing on emotional literacy, resilience and healthy habits, helping pupils build the foundations for lifelong wellbeing.
Pupil Voice & Leadership
Every pupil at Swanbourne House is an anti-bullying ambassador, living out our Swanbourne Way values of Kindness, Curiosity, and Effort.
Our Student Council, elected from Years 2–8, meets half-termly to champion pupil voice in areas such as mental health, wellbeing, charity work, play, and enrichment.
Leadership roles, including School Captains, Prefects, and Heads of Houses, play an active part in fostering a supportive and inclusive school community, ensuring that every child feels a strong sense of belonging.

Science
Science
Our outstanding facilities provide the perfect environment for hands-on learning, collaboration and discovery in Science. From Year 5, pupils study Science in one of our fully-equipped, dedicated laboratories by a subject specialist. Practical experiments and investigations grow in complexity as children move through the school, helping them to develop a strong grasp of scientific principles while learning about the discoveries of the world’s greatest scientists.
Modern-day problem solving
Pupils are inspired to use their scientific learning as a lens through which to explore and tackle some of the world’s most pressing challenges. From climate change to plastic pollution and global health, lessons go beyond facts and formulas to develop curiosity, critical thinking, and problem-solving skills. Enrichment opportunities such as Science competitions, field trips, and opportunities to interact with leading scientists bring these issues to life, enabling pupils to connect their classroom learning with real-world innovation and solutions.

Book a visit
Choosing the right school is a big decision — and there’s no better way to get a feel for Swanbourne than by visiting in person. Complete the form below and we’ll arrange a tour and meeting with our Head at a time that suits your family.
Senior School Pathways
Choosing the right senior school is one of the most important steps in your child’s educational journey. At Swanbourne House, we are proud of our strong record in preparing pupils for success at a wide range of leading day and boarding schools across the UK.
Through our membership of The Stowe Group, pupils benefit from a pathway to Stowe, including fee discounts and access to world-class facilities. For families exploring other options, our pupils also achieve places and scholarships at many prestigious independent schools across Buckinghamshire, Northamptonshire, Oxfordshire and beyond.
Our dedicated Mentoring Programme provides specialist support for those excelling in academics, sport, drama, art, music, and design & technology, ensuring pupils are prepared for senior school assessments and scholarship opportunities.

Mentoring Programme

Book a visit

Art
Art at Swanbourne House nurtures creativity by linking contemporary practice with rich artistic traditions.
From Year 3 onwards, pupils enjoy specialist art lessons in our dedicated studio, where they develop strong observational drawing skills and explore colour, texture, form and space.
Hands-on experience is central to our approach. Pupils work across painting, sculpture, collage, ceramics, printing, textiles, and digital art, encouraging both experimentation and refinement. Inspiration comes not only from the classroom but also through visits to galleries and museums and encounters with practising artists and designers.
Exhibitions and Showcases
Our Art Department hosts major exhibitions twice a year, celebrating pupils’ best work. Pupils also contribute to prestigious external events such as the Stowe Art Exhibition.
Art Clubs and Enrichment
Creative opportunities extend beyond the classroom. From age five, children can join pottery, textiles, and crafts clubs. As they progress through the Middle and Upper School, pupils take part in regular Art Clubs and Saturday enrichment sessions.
Pupils on scholarship pathways to Senior School are also prepared for art scholarships in our dedicated mentoring programme.

Computing
Computing at Swanbourne House
Computing provides pupils with a strong foundation in Computer Science, Digital Literacy and Information Technology. In the Early Years, learning is introduced through exploration and play, nurturing curiosity and creativity from the very start. From Year 2 onwards, pupils benefit from access to designated computing suites, giving them the tools and space to develop their skills in a structured way. The Computing Department also enriches learning through a weekly Code Club, where children can explore creative coding projects in a fun and joyful environment.
It is a hands-on and imaginative subject, where pupils are encouraged to problem-solve, collaborate and apply their knowledge in practical contexts. As they grow in confidence and experience, pupils progress from block-based programming to more sophisticated text-based languages, developing confidence in writing and debugging their own code. They explore physical computing through Micro:bits and Raspberry Pis, as well as creative applications such as coding in Minecraft. A strong focus is also placed on online safety and responsible digital behaviour, ensuring pupils learn how to navigate the digital world with confidence and care.

Book a visit
Choosing the right school is a big decision — and there’s no better way to get a feel for Swanbourne than by visiting in person. Complete the form below and we’ll arrange a tour and meeting with our Head at a time that suits your family.
English
At Swanbourne House, our English programme is aimed at nurturing a love of literature and language. By Year 8, pupils will have studied a wide range of poets, playwrights, and historical texts, from Beowulf to Shakespeare, and from John Agard to Dylan Thomas.
We encourage a passion for reading through weekly sessions that provide quiet time for students to immerse themselves in books. Supported by Accelerated Reader, we help recommend suitable and challenging texts for each student.
Our focus is on developing strong writing and communication skills, through both formal and creative writing tasks. Pupils also grow in confidence with written and oral presentations, using ICT alongside traditional handwriting to express their ideas. Spelling, punctuation, and grammar are taught thoroughly to meet and exceed curriculum standards.
Creative writing and constructive feedback are central to our teaching, ensuring every student reflects, improves, and progresses in their skills, with regular spelling tests to reinforce learning.

Book a visit
Choosing the right school is a big decision — and there’s no better way to get a feel for Swanbourne than by visiting in person. Complete the form below and we’ll arrange a tour and meeting with our Head at a time that suits your family.
Humanities
Geography, History and Religious Studies are taught within our Humanities Department, with specialist teaching from Year 5. Knowledge and key skills are learnt in context through varied and exciting projects the pupils undertake each term. The study of Humanities provokes pupils to ask questions about their relationship with the environment, local area and with other cultures and faiths around the globe.
Geography
Geography at Swanbourne House encourages pupils to explore and understand the world around them. Through practical enquiry and engaging topics, children investigate the relationships between people, places and environments, developing a sense of curiosity about how our planet works.
Pupils study physical and human geography. Topics include rivers and coasts, weather and climate, ecosystems, urbanisation, migration and sustainability. Lessons combine maps, data and digital resources with practical fieldwork, giving pupils the chance to test ideas and experience geography first-hand.
Pupils take part in local field trips as well as larger excursions, such as to Dorset and Iceland, giving them the opportunity to apply classroom knowledge in real-world settings.
History
From the local history of Swanbourne, to the Middle Ages and Vikings, to the Tudors, Victorians and World Wars, pupils study British and world history in depth. They learn to evaluate evidence, interpret different viewpoints, and understand change over time.
Learning extends beyond the classroom with visits to historic sites and museums, including trips to Warwick Castle, Bletchley Park and a History of Witchcraft tour in London, helping pupils connect directly with the past.
Re-enactments, including our annual Trench-digging workshops, and themed events (our summer school water fight is always based on a historic battle!), enrich the curriculum, making history engaging and memorable.
Religious Studies (RS)
RS at Swanbourne House encourages pupils to explore life’s big questions while developing respect and understanding for different cultures and beliefs. Lessons are engaging, discussion-based and designed to nurture curiosity, empathy and moral awareness.
Pupils study the major world religions – including Christianity, Islam, Judaism, Hinduism, Buddhism and Sikhism – alongside ethical and philosophical questions. They learn about traditions, festivals and teachings, while reflecting on how faith influences communities across the world.
Debate and reflection are central to RS lessons. Pupils explore moral and ethical dilemmas from fairness and justice to environmental responsibility.

Leavers' Destinations & Scholarships
Leavers’ Destinations
At Swanbourne House, we are proud of the strong academic foundations and wide-ranging talents our pupils develop. Year after year, our leavers move on to some of the UK’s leading independent schools, reflecting the confidence, skills, and ambition nurtured here.
In recent years, Swanbourne House pupils have successfully secured places at:
St Albans High School
11+ Academic Scholarships
Application for the 11+ Scholarship are made in Year 6, whether your child is already part of our family at Swanbourne House, or at another school.
Pupils will be awarded the Scholarship for Years 7 and 8, with the intention of progressing to Stowe School at Year 9. The candidate will follow the Academic Scholarship pathway at Swanbourne House and afterwards at Stowe.

Our History
Gallery
Look back at over a century of history and events at Swanbourne House, then explore our gallery of photographs for a glimpse into the past.
1920
Lionel and Margaret Evans bring 43 boys to Swanbourne House from Bradfield College. Dress code for the first 30 years is Norfolk Jackets and knee-breeches during the week and Eton suits on Sundays. There are rarely more than two cars on site and boarders travel by train to and from school; their trunks and play boxes are brought up from Swanbourne station on a horse-drawn carrier’s cart.
1925
The first swimming pool is opened, measuring 36 x 20ft, and the temperature set at a very cool 16.5°C. F. Scott Fitzgerald’s iconic novel, The Great Gatsby, is published and John Logie Baird builds the first television transmitter. More and more airlines are formed around the world for freight mail and passenger traffic. Stanley Baldwin is the UK’s Prime Minister.
1947
Lionel Evans retires and is succeeded by his eldest son, Harold Evans, as Headmaster. The United Nations Charter creates The United Nations. Harry S Truman becomes US President following the death of President Roosevelt. Animal Farm by George Orwell is published and later becomes one of the most revered novels of the 20th century.
1950
Portable radios and crystal sets begin to appear around the school and Sunday evening film shows are introduced at Swanbourne showing Buster Keaton, Charlie Chaplin and Laurel and Hardy. Defining literature of the time includes; The Catcher in the Rye, J. D. Salinger, (1951); Charlotte’s Web, E.B. White, (1952); and Lord of the Flies, William Golding, (1954). Clement Attlee is Prime Minister of the United Kingdom.
1965
The Science Laboratory at Swanbourne is refurbished. The state funeral of Sir Winston Churchill takes place in London with the largest assembly of statesmen in the world. The Rolling Stones are on a world tour and US President Lyndon Johnson takes the Oath of Office for a second and final time.
1970
Swanbourne House School becomes a Charitable Trust. Concorde’s first supersonic flight goes into service. The Beatles disband and the Apollo 13 mission successfully attempts a ‘splashdown’ in the Pacific Ocean after the famous emergency call, “Houston, we have a problem”.
1971
Improvements are made to the playing fields, staff accommodation, tennis courts, stage, music room, art room and scout huts. At the same time, NASA’s Apollo 14 becomes the third successful manned mission to the moon. Edward Heath becomes Prime Minister after winning the 1970 general election and the UK and Ireland switch to decimal currency.
1972
The Paddock is cleared, levelled and drained to create the playing field we see today. The first scientific hand-held calculator (HP-35) is introduced. Rose Heilbron becomes the first female Judge at the Old Bailey in London. The Watergate Scandal grips America and leads to a constitutional crisis.
1974
Harold Evans retires as Headmaster and Geoffrey Jameson takes up tenure. US President Richard Nixon resigns his presidency following Watergate and Britain enters its first postwar recession. The Heimlich Manoeuvre for rescuing choking victims is first published in a medial journal. The Sears Tower in Chicago becomes the worlds tallest building and Isabel Peron, President of Argentina, becomes the first female president in the world.
1979
The first four day girls arrive at Swanbourne House. China institutes the one child per family rule, General Knowledge Quiz Game, Trivial Pursuit, is launched and Pink Floyd release the seminal album ‘The Wall’. For the first time in history a female, Margaret Thatcher, is elected Prime Minister in the UK after a landslide General Election. Sony releases ‘The Walkman’ a worldwide success costing $200.
1981
The first computer is bought for the school, a Commodore P.E.T. (Personal Electronic Transactor) which is the first personal computer to be sold to the public. Prince Charles marries Lady Diana Spencer, the first London Marathon is held and MS-DOS is released by Microsoft along with the first IBM PC. Ronald Reagan becomes US President and Rupert Murdoch shuts down The Sunday Times due to an industrial dispute.
1982
Tom More takes up the reins as Headmaster. The Falklands War dominates international news. Founder of Apple, Steve Jobs, turns his attention to appropriating the current Macintosh, the first mass-market personal computer that featured a graphical user interface, built-in screen and mouse.
1983
Swanbourne House opens the Pre-Prep Department. Britain’s Conservative Government, led by Margaret Thatcher, is re-elected by a landslide majority and Neil Kinnock is elected leader of the Labour Party. The world’s most popular word processing programme, Microsoft Word, is launched and IBM releases the IBM PC XT.
1984
The Evans building is opened. Virgin Atlantic Airways makes its inaugural flight, Bishop Desmond Tutu wins The Nobel Peace Prize and DNA profiling is developed. Following the widespread famine in Ethiopia, British and Irish pop stars join together under the name ‘Band Aid’ and record the song ‘Do They Know It’s Christmas.’ British miners go on strike to protest at pit closures.
1986
Swanbourne House Nursery is opened. Space Shuttle ‘Challenger‘ disintegrates 73 seconds after launch from the United States, killing the crew of seven astronauts, including schoolteacher Christa McAuliffe. Sir Andrew Lloyd Webber premieres Phantom of the Opera at the Her Majesty’s Theatre in London.
1987
The Fremantle Technology Building is opened. Terry Waite, the special envoy of the Archbishop of Canterbury, is kidnapped in Beirut. The first criminal conviction using DNA evidence is made. Work on the Channel Tunnel begins and The Single European Act (SEA) becomes effective, setting the goal for the European Economic Community to join together to form a single market with a single currency by the end of 1992.
1996
Tom More retires. Stephen and Julie Goodhart are appointed as Joint Heads. A new all-weather sports area (the Red Astro) is installed. Prince Charles and Diana, Princess of Wales divorce. DVD’s are launched in Japan and the number of users on the Internet exceeds 10 million. E-bay is launched and the first ever cloning of a mammal, Dolly the sheep, grips the nation.
1997
The Stable House, a new Nursery building, and two new boarding dormitories open. JK Rowling releases Harry Potter and the Philosopher’s Stone. Tony Blair is elected the first Labour Prime Minister since James Callaghan in 1976 and Princess Diana is killed in a car crash in Paris. Great Britain hands Hong Kong back to China.
1998
. After many years of troubles in Northern Ireland both sides agree to the Good Friday Peace Agreement. The Soviet Union banking system suffers a meltdown when the Rouble loses 70% of its value against the US dollar in 6 months with several of the largest Russian banks collapsing. Titanic becomes the first film to gross $1billion.
2001
The Walker building is opened. The indoor swimming pool is opened. Terrorists attack the United States using hijacked passenger aircraft to bring down the Twin Towers in New York and crashing an aircraft into the Pentagon in Arlington County, Virginia. The attacks become known simply as ‘9/11’ due to the date of the attack, September 11th. America declares ‘A War on Terrorism’ and invades Afghanistan.
2010
The school celebrates its 90th Anniversary and a new astro-turf pitch (the Green Astro) is opened. Apple releases the new iPhone 4 but problems with antenna design cause consumer problems. Apple also release the iPad taking the new technology of touch screen computing to new levels. A magnitude 7 earthquake hits Haiti and devastates the country. The Burj Khalifa skyscraper in Dubai opens and becomes the world’s tallest building.
2013
The Goodharts retire and Simon Hitchings takes over as Headmaster. There is a complete refurbishment of the Chapel and Front Hall. President Barrack Hussein Obama III is inaugurated for his second term in US office. North Korea continues missile and nuclear tests despite international pressure, increasing tension with the rest of the world. The House of Commons votes 400 to 175 in favour of the Bill to legalise same-sex marriage in England and Wales.
2015
The Music Department is redesigned and fully refurbished with a purpose built teaching room, a number of practice rooms, a percussion room and purpose-built instrument storage lockers. Work also begins on refurbishing Cloisters and Pre-Prep and all classrooms in these areas are equipped with ‘Clevertouch’ boards. The Walker Building is also refurbished including an expansion of the IT suite. A general election in the UK results in the first Conservative majority government in 18 years. There is a refugee crisis in Europe as tens of thousands of people flee war-torn Syria.
2017
The Fremantle Building is re-designed and re-opened as an all-encompassing STEAM faculty. Donald Trump is sworn in as the 45th President of the United States. Trump is the first person to be elected President of the United States who was neither a political office holder nor a military general. In the midst of Brexit, a snap general election is held in the UK resulting in a hung parliament with the Conservative party, led by Prime Minister Theresa May, losing their majority.
2018
The 7th Head, Mrs Jane Thorpe, takes up tenure leading Swanbourne House School into its centenary and a defining new chapter in the school’s history. An ISI Inspection confirms the school’s provision to be ‘Excellent’ in all areas.
2019
Swanbourne replaces compulsory Saturday morning academic lessons with an Enrichment Programme . The PSB (Pre Senior Baccalaureate) assessment framework is introduced, replacing Common Entrance examinations. An Outdoor Learning classroom is installed in the grounds and an extensive Outdoor Learning Programme is introduced into the curriculum.
2020
Swanbourne House School celebrates its centenary year. The country faces lockdown during the global Covid-19 pandemic.
2021
Swanbourne House forms The Stowe Group, with Stowe and Winchester House. Membership of The Stowe Group gives Swanbourne House pupils access to a combined site of over 800 acres with unrivalled educational and co-curricular facilities. These include Stowe’s Worsley Science Centre, the Roxburgh Theatre, the Chung Music School, state-of-the-art gym, eight lane athletics track, Equestrian Centre, six lane competition swimming pool, clay pigeon shooting range and golf course. 2021 brings a major global rollout of COVID-19 vaccines. Rescheduled Olympic Games takes place in Tokyo. Prince Philip, Duke of Edinburgh dies.
2022
The school sees significant investment from The Stowe Group, including The Fort (a new play area for the Manor House), the updating of the Walled Astroturf and a Boarding House refurbishment. The country enters a period of mourning after Her Majesty Queen Elizabeth II dies after 70 years on the throne.
2023
Mr Nick Holloway joins the school as the 8th Head of Swanbourne House.

Book a visit
Choosing the right school is a big decision — and there’s no better way to get a feel for Swanbourne than by visiting in person. Complete the form below and we’ll arrange a tour and meeting with our Head at a time that suits your family.
Pre-Reception
High-Quality Early Years Teaching
Our Pre-Reception class (Nursery age 3+) provides the perfect start to your child’s educational journey, welcoming children into the Swanbourne House community ahead of their move into Reception. With small classes (maximum 16), expert teaching and access to our outstanding facilities, we offer a nurturing, inspiring environment where children thrive.
Mornings are led by a fully qualified EYFS Teacher, supported by a Teaching Assistant, focusing on early reading, phonics, writing and maths through fun, meaningful activities, giving children strong foundations for academic success.
Afternoon sessions allow children to explore their interests, embed their learning, and grow in independence. This balance of structured teaching and play nurtures both academic foundations and social skills giving pupils a confident step into Reception.
Outdoor Learning
Our Pre-Reception (Nursery) children enjoy their own garden overlooking St Swithun’s Church, as well as access to Swanbourne’s 55-acre school grounds.
Outdoor play, exploration and discovery are at the heart of our approach – whether in the dedicated Pre-Reception Garden, the Eucalyptus woods, or the wider school woodland. Every week brings new adventures, from bug-hunting and den building to our much-loved nature walks to the golf course. These experiences help nurture curiosity, confidence, and a lifelong love of the outdoors.
Co-Curricular
We know the importance of a balanced day, and as such families have a rich array of co-curricular activities, including yoga, multi-skills, balance bikes, cricket, football, and performing arts, to choose from.
Specialist Teaching
Children also benefit from specialist lessons in Music, Sport and Outdoor Learning, helping them develop creativity, coordination, and confidence from the very start of their school life.
Flexible Wraparound Care
We know flexibility matters to families. Our wraparound care starts at 7.30am and runs until 6.30pm daily, making Swanbourne House an ideal choice for busy parents looking for an independent school nursery in Buckinghamshire or Milton Keynes.
Funding & Places
From the term following their third birthday, your child is eligible for the universal funded entitlement.
A minimum of seven sessions per week is recommended, with priority given to full-time places. See our Fees page for more information.
What’s in a Pine Cone?
Creativity and curiosity is really at the heart of our Pre-Reception. We use the example of a simple pine cone and how it has boundless possibilities. As children explore, the pine cone could transform into a crucial component to fix an imaginary car, or be a key ingredient in a creation within the mud kitchen. The magic lies not just in the object itself but in the imaginative journey our youngest Swanbournians are encouraged to take.
The Stowe Group
We’re a proud member of The Stowe Group and our Pre- Reception children are the very youngest pupils in the Group. As the children progress through the school - whether they eventually move on to Stowe or elsewhere - they will benefit from the huge array of opportunities that being part of the Group offers.
